summary: Bind the twin lifecycle blueprint standard

delivery.outcome: A conforming profile must pin the immutable lifecycle blueprint revision its declared lifecycle trait operates under, so the stage graph behind LifecycleBlueprintRef is a reviewed contract instead of an unmodelled assertion
nonGoals: No stage-graph validator inside twin; wellmanifest/twin-lifecycle owns blueprint graph rules and their TWINLC diagnostics
No protobuf change; LifecycleBlueprintRef already carries the reference fields
No new required trait, operation, transport binding or runtime dependency
No blueprint content, stage list or approver identity embedded in the twin profile
No claim that a lifecycle gate, approval or blueprint reference grants execution authority

architecture.decision: Add wellmanifest/twin-lifecycle as a required normative contract source and require $.lifecycle.blueprintRef to pin one immutable blueprint revision by definition URI and canonical sha256 digest; keep graph semantics in the external standard and correct the transferred lifecycle-dsl repository URL to its current immutable location
architecture.rollback: Revert ticket-006; profiles without $.lifecycle.blueprintRef remain identifiable by the prior profile version and contract hashes

validation.evidence: The reference profile pins the twin-lifecycle standard revision plus artifact digest and one immutable blueprint revision, and validates with exit status 0
Mutation tests reject a missing, mutable, malformed or unpinned blueprint reference and a missing twin-lifecycle source contract with stable TWIN-LIFECYCLE-001 and TWIN-SOURCE-001 diagnostics

commands: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m twin_standard generate profiles/generic-twin.json --out /tmp/twin-006 --language rust
validation.evidence: The generated transport map carries the pinned blueprint reference and generation stays byte-identical for equal inputs
Host, networkless Docker and governance pass within four implementation files and no runtime dependencies
